title: descriptors
description: Hub to phone, after `welcome` when both sides have the `descriptors` capability, and again whenever a hub Bucket comes, goes or changes. Each one is a full snapshot: it replaces every Descriptor the hub sent before. The phone caches the latest snapshot.

buckets.description: Every Bucket the hub's Providers publish, one Descriptor each. Ids are unique within a snapshot.

descriptor.description: One Bucket, described for the phone. The phone never runs Provider code; it runs the Primitives named here.

id.description: Stable across connections and hub restarts; the key the phone caches the Bucket under and addresses it by.

name.description: What the loop says for the Bucket. It always counts as an alias.

aliases.description: Further phrases that name the Bucket.

type.description: The kind of Bucket. Known in v1.0: `agent`, `hub`. A phone treats a type it does not know like any other Bucket, by its Primitives.

primitives.description: The Primitives this Bucket uses. Known in v1.0: `note`, `draft`, `speak_item`, `request`. A phone that does not know one of them keeps only the Bucket's `request` commands, and the loop says so once.

commands.description: The phrases that are commands while the Bucket has Focus (or whatever has Focus, with `anywhere`), in a deterministic grammar.

dialog.description: The dialog an agent Bucket is blocked on, while it is (#80); absent when it is not known to wait on one. Only a `question` can be answered by voice (rung 4 of the ladder), with the `draft` Primitive's option commands and a `send` carrying an `answer`. A `permission` prompt is rung 5 and is never answered; nor is an `unknown` dialog (the hub sees the agent blocked but cannot tell on what, as with herdr and no Claude Code hooks), nor one of a kind the phone does not know. A phone that does not know this field cannot answer dialogs.

kind.description: Known in v1.0: `question` (Claude Code's AskUserQuestion), `permission`, `unknown`. A phone treats any other kind as `unknown`.

id.description: For a `question`: which dialog this is. A `send` that answers it names it, and the hub refuses an answer to a dialog that is no longer the open one.

questions.description: For a `question`: its questions, in the order they are answered.

question.description: The question, as the agent asked it.

options.description: The options' labels, in order: "option one" is the first.

multi_select.description: True: the agent lets the person pick several options (by voice, one is picked). Absent means false.

other.description: True: the question also takes a free-text answer, which a `send`'s choice carries as `text`. Absent means false.

id.description: Unique within the Descriptor; what the phone sends back to name the command.

phrases.description: What the person says. The first is the canonical phrase.

primitive.description: The Primitive that runs the command, one of the Descriptor's `primitives`. The phone runs a `request` command by sending a `request` naming the Descriptor's `id` and the command's `id`, and speaks the `reply`.

anywhere.description: True: the phrase is a command whatever has Focus ("what's blocked"), not only while this Bucket has it. Absent means false. A phone that does not know this field hears the command only under the Bucket's Focus.

reply_within_ms.description: For a `request` command: how long the phone waits for its `reply`, in milliseconds, before it says the hub did not answer. Absent means the phone's default (5 s). The hub sets it for a command that takes longer to answer ("what does it say", which asks a model). A phone waits at least its default whatever the value, and may wait less than a long value asks (the v1 phone caps it at 60 s); one that does not know this field waits its default.
